<b>Эйкозаноиды</b> — местные гормоны из: Eicosanoids are local hormones made from arachidonic acid (20 carbon atoms, hence “eicosa-”). Upon injury or inflammation, phospholipase A₂ cleaves it off a membrane phospholipid. Then there are two pathways. Cyclooxygenase (COX-1 is always active, COX-2 is switched on in inflammation) makes PGH₂, and from it come prostaglandin E₂ (pain, fever, swelling, protection of the stomach), prostacyclin (endothelium: dilates vessels, prevents clots) and thromboxane A₂ (platelets: makes them stick together, constricts vessels). 5-Lipoxygenase makes leukotrienes: B₄ attracts neutrophils, C₄ and D₄ constrict the bronchi. Eicosanoids live for seconds to minutes and act close to where they are made.
<b>Аспирин</b> ацетилирует серин в канал: Aspirin acetylates a serine in the COX channel — irreversibly: the enzyme stays switched off for the rest of the molecule’s life. All prostaglandins and thromboxane fall: pain, fever and inflammation subside, and platelets stick together less. Part of the arachidonic acid is diverted into the lipoxygenase pathway — in some people this means more leukotrienes and asthma attacks.
<b>Ибупрофен</b> (и диклофенак, напроксе: Ibuprofen (as well as diclofenac and naproxen) occupies the COX channel reversibly, competing with arachidonic acid; after a few hours the drug leaves and the enzyme works again. It blocks both COX-1 and COX-2 — hence the side effects on the stomach and kidneys.
<b>Целекоксиб</b> избирательно блокирует: Celecoxib selectively blocks COX-2, the inflammatory isoform. The stomach (COX-1) suffers less. But endothelial COX-2 makes prostacyclin, while platelets make their thromboxane with COX-1 — the balance shifts toward clotting, and the risk of heart attacks and strokes rises (one of the coxibs, rofecoxib, was withdrawn from the market).
<b>Глюкокортикоиды</b> (преднизолон, дек: Glucocorticoids (prednisolone, dexamethasone) act further upstream: through a nuclear receptor they switch on the synthesis of annexin-1, which inhibits phospholipase A₂, and they suppress the COX-2 gene. No arachidonic acid means neither prostaglandins nor leukotrienes. That is why they also help in asthma, where NSAIDs are powerless.
<b>Баланс в сосуде.</b> Тромбоциты делаю: Balance in the vessel. Platelets make thromboxane A₂ (COX-1): it makes them stick together at the site of injury (collagen of the wall) and constricts the vessel. Healthy endothelium releases prostacyclin: it dilates the vessel and keeps platelets from clumping where the wall is intact. As long as the two are in balance, a clot grows only where it is needed.
<b>Малая доза аспирина</b> (75–150 мг в: Low-dose aspirin (75–150 mg per day). A platelet has no nucleus — it cannot make new COX, so it produces no thromboxane for the rest of its life (7–10 days). Endothelial cells, which have nuclei, resynthesize COX within hours, so prostacyclin is largely preserved. The result is fewer clots: this is how repeat heart attacks and strokes are prevented. The price is bleeding and a risk of ulcers.
<b>Большая доза аспирина</b> (обезболива: High-dose aspirin (analgesic doses, grams per day) also suppresses COX in the endothelium: there is less prostacyclin too, so the protection against clots does not increase, while the risk of bleeding and ulcers does.
<b>Отмена аспирина.</b> Тромбоксан возвр: Stopping aspirin. Thromboxane returns gradually, as the bone marrow releases new platelets (about 10% per day). That is why aspirin is stopped 5–7 days before elective surgery.
<b>Где работают простагландины.</b> В ги: Where prostaglandins work. In the hypothalamus, PGE₂ raises the temperature “set point” — fever. At the site of inflammation it sensitizes nerve endings — pain — and dilates vessels — redness and swelling. In the stomach it protects the mucosa (mucus, bicarbonate, blood flow), in the kidneys it maintains blood flow, and in the uterus it causes contractions (menstrual cramps, labor). In the bronchi, leukotrienes cause spasm.
<b>НПВС</b> (ибупрофен, диклофенак) убир: NSAIDs (ibuprofen, diclofenac) relieve fever, pain and inflammation, but they also remove the useful prostaglandins: stomach ulcers and bleeding (red spot), reduced renal blood flow (especially with dehydration, or together with diuretics and ACE inhibitors), fluid retention. They relieve menstrual cramps.
<b>Аспирин</b>: то же, что НПВС, плюс не: Aspirin: the same as NSAIDs, plus an irreversible effect on platelets. In some people with asthma and nasal polyps it causes severe bronchospasm — “aspirin asthma” (aspirin-exacerbated respiratory disease; more leukotrienes). Aspirin is not given to children with viral infections because of Reye syndrome (liver and brain damage).
<b>Коксибы</b> снимают воспаление и боль: Coxibs relieve inflammation and pain while sparing the stomach (COX-1 keeps working), but they raise the risk of thrombosis; the kidneys can suffer as well, since COX-2 is present there.
<b>Парацетамол</b> снижает жар и боль, д: Paracetamol (acetaminophen) reduces fever and pain, acting mainly in the brain (where there are few peroxides and it can inhibit COX), but it barely relieves inflammation and does not affect the stomach or platelets. It is dangerous in overdose — to the liver (see the “Liver” topic).
Из одной жирной кислоты мембраны клетка: From a single fatty acid of the membrane, a cell makes signals for pain, fever, clotting and spasm within seconds — and aspirin and ibuprofen switch off one enzyme on this pathway.
\n <div><h2>Эйкозаноиды</h2>\n:
Eicosanoids

Derivatives of polyunsaturated C₂₀ acids (arachidonic, ω-6; eicosapentaenoic, ω-3). Prostanoids (prostaglandins, prostacyclin, thromboxanes) come from the cyclooxygenase pathway; leukotrienes and lipoxins from the lipoxygenase pathway; epoxides from cytochromes P450. They act through G protein–coupled receptors (EP1–EP4, IP, TP, BLT, CysLT), locally, and break down within seconds to minutes.

COX-1 and COX-2

COX-1 is constitutive (stomach, kidneys, platelets); COX-2 is inducible (inflammation: cytokines, endotoxin), but it is also present in the endothelium, kidneys and brain. The enzyme is bifunctional: cyclooxygenase (arachidonic acid → PGG₂) and peroxidase (PGG₂ → PGH₂).

Drugs

  • NSAIDs: aspirin (irreversible), ibuprofen, diclofenac, naproxen (reversible); coxibs are COX-2-selective.
  • Glucocorticoids act on phospholipase A₂ and the COX-2 gene.
  • Antileukotrienes: montelukast (CysLT₁ receptor), zileuton (5-LOX) — for asthma.
  • Prostaglandin analogues: misoprostol (stomach protection, obstetrics), latanoprost (glaucoma), alprostadil (patent ductus arteriosus in newborns).

  • The molecules follow their chemical formulas; the enzymes are schematic blobs, and the membrane and vessel are schematic.
  • Eicosanoid levels and platelet counts are a qualitative model; the time course after stopping aspirin is compressed.

ТТГ (лог.), св. T₄; серое — норма: TSH (log), free T₄; gray = normal range
<b>Аутоиммунный тиреоидит Хашимото</b> —: Hashimoto’s autoimmune thyroiditis is the most common cause of hypothyroidism. Lymphocytes destroy the gland, T₄ falls, the feedback weakens, and the pituitary releases more and more TSH — high TSH, low T₄. Metabolism slows down: fatigue, cold intolerance, weight gain, dry skin, swelling, slow pulse, constipation, depression. (Congenital hypothyroidism — most often due to an underdeveloped gland — leads to cretinism if untreated, which is why all newborns are screened for TSH.)
<b>Болезнь Грейвса</b> (диффузный токсич: Graves’ disease (diffuse toxic goiter). The immune system makes antibodies to the TSH receptor (purple) that activate it without any TSH. The gland enlarges and works nonstop, and feedback silences the pituitary — TSH near zero, high T₄. Palpitations, sweating, tremor, weight loss despite a good appetite, irritability; unlike other forms of thyrotoxicosis, also bulging eyes (Graves’ ophthalmopathy).
<b>Тиамазол</b> и пропилтиоурацил блокир: Methimazole (thiamazole) and propylthiouracil block thyroid peroxidase — iodine is no longer attached to thyroglobulin, and T₄ falls to normal (after long suppression, TSH takes months to recover). Other options are radioactive iodine (the gland takes it up itself and is destroyed) or surgery; the fast pulse is brought down with β-blockers.
<b>Мало йода в пище</b>: йодида в крови: Too little iodine in the diet: there is little iodide in the blood — NIS (of which there is even more under the influence of TSH) captures less, tyrosines are iodinated more slowly, and the share of MIT and T₃ grows — the gland economizes on iodine. Less hormone is released, and the pituitary responds by raising TSH (“Axis and diseases” mode).
<b>Много T₃</b> (тиреотоксикоз): клетки: High T₃ (thyrotoxicosis): cells burn fuel wastefully, a lot of heat is produced, and the metabolic rate rises one and a half to two times; the heart beats faster, partly because T₃ adds β-adrenergic receptors and directly switches on cardiac muscle genes.
<b>Клубочковая зона</b> — только здесь е: The zona glomerulosa is the only zone with aldosterone synthase, and it lacks 17α-hydroxylase. It is stimulated by angiotensin II and a rise in blood K⁺ (ACTH only weakly). Aldosterone makes the kidneys retain Na⁺ and water and excrete K⁺, so blood pressure rises.
<b>Сетчатая зона</b> — <b>17,20-лиаза</b: In the zona reticularis, 17,20-lyase cleaves off the entire side chain, producing androgens: DHEA (mostly as its sulfate, DHEA-S) and androstenedione. In women this is the main source of androgens; in men most testosterone is made by the testes.
<b>Синдром Кушинга</b> — избыток кортизо: Cushing’s syndrome is an excess of cortisol (glucocorticoids taken as medication, or a tumor of the adrenal gland or the pituitary). Shown here is the adrenal tumor variant — ACTH is suppressed; in Cushing’s disease (a pituitary tumor), by contrast, ACTH is high. High glucose (steroid diabetes), obesity of the face and trunk with thin arms and legs, stretch marks, osteoporosis, hypertension, weakened immunity. With an adrenal tumor, ACTH is suppressed by feedback.
<b>Как стероид включает ген.</b> Стероид: How a steroid switches on a gene. Steroids are fat-soluble and cross the membrane on their own. Inside, nuclear receptors await them; shown here is the real ligand-binding domain (without the DNA-binding domain) of the progesterone receptor with progesterone in its pocket (PDB 1A28). The hormone closes the pocket with helix 12 (pink), a coactivator (purple) binds to it, and together they switch on genes on DNA. The receptors for cortisol (GR), aldosterone (MR), androgens and estrogens are built the same way.
<b>Врождённая гиперплазия коры</b> (дефи: Congenital adrenal hyperplasia (21-hydroxylase deficiency, about 1 in 10,000–15,000 newborns). Cortisol is low, and in ~3/4 of patients aldosterone is low too (the salt-wasting form); the precursor 17-OH-progesterone accumulates (it is the basis of the diagnosis, including newborn screening) and is diverted into androgens. With little cortisol, the pituitary pours out ACTH and the cortex enlarges. Girls show signs of androgen excess already at birth, and some children have life-threatening salt wasting. Treatment: hydrocortisone and, if needed, fludrocortisone.
\n <div><h2>Стероидные гормоны</h2>:
Steroid hormones

All steroids are cholesterol derivatives with four rings (cyclopentanoperhydrophenanthrene). The enzymes of steroidogenesis are mostly cytochromes P450 (CYP11A1, CYP17, CYP21, CYP11B1, CYP11B2) in the mitochondria and ER. Cholesterol is carried into the mitochondrion by the StAR protein — this is the rate-limiting step, and ACTH speeds it up via cAMP.

Regulation

  • Aldosterone — the renin–angiotensin system and K⁺.
  • Cortisol — ACTH, the circadian rhythm (peak in the morning), stress; feedback on the hypothalamus and pituitary.
  • Medullary catecholamines — sympathetic nerves (acetylcholine); epinephrine synthesis (PNMT) requires cortisol — it arrives from the cortex through portal vessels, and its concentration in the medulla is tens of times higher than in the general circulation.

Glucocorticoids as drugs

Prednisolone and dexamethasone suppress inflammation and immunity (phospholipase A₂, cytokines). Long-term use causes Cushing’s syndrome and suppression of the body’s own adrenal cortex, so they are withdrawn gradually.
